A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Project-Probe-Aggregate (PPA) research. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-C are readable and complete enough for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PPA experiments on five benchmarks, including accuracy comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Section 6 and Appendix B, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The projection, pseudo-group identification, group logit adjustment, and weight aggregation procedures are unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1. The prompt-tuning and adapter variants are also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Waterbirds, CelebA, MetaShift, BAR, and Living-17 with the same tasks, groups, and test scenarios (Section 6.1 and Appendix B).

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the main and appendix experiments, including the methods in Tables 2-3 and the B2T comparison in Table 11.

E3.justification: The backbones, data handling, 100-epoch training budget, evaluation metrics, checkpoint-selection rules, and hyperparameter settings remain unchanged (Section 6.3 and Appendix B).

E4.justification: The component ablations, architecture and fine-tuning studies, estimated-group analysis, hyperparameter sensitivity, and pseudo-label noise analysis are all retained without revision (Section 6.5 and Appendix B).

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or formal significance tests. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 2 retains PPA's CLIP ResNet-50 worst-group accuracies of 84.3%, 91.1%, and 90.8% on Waterbirds, CelebA, and MetaShift, respectively; appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, Propositions 1-2, and their derivations and proofs in Section 5 and Appendix A are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient group robustness without training group labels, improved minority-group identification, and Bayes optimality for balanced group error.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, worst-group versus average-accuracy tradeoff, and Appendix C's limitation concerning insufficient CLIP knowledge for downstream tasks are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same optimizer, learning-rate schedule, batch sizes, prompt templates, hyperparameter search range, and NVIDIA A6000 hardware information. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the comparisons with prior research, and the reference entries are unchanged. There is no revised novelty positioning or citation addition.

P1.justification: v3 adds a footnote describing Beier Zhu's visit to AGI Lab and identifying Chi Zhang as corresponding author. It also expands the funding acknowledgment to name Alibaba-NTU Global e-Sustainability CorpLab; scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The new first-page footnote causes minor text reflow across pages 1-5, and the expanded acknowledgment shifts reference layout on page 9. Figures, tables, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies author and funding attribution, while retaining the same scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations. The small layout shifts do not materially improve or impair readability, so there is no meaningful overall quality difference.
